summary: Customer is evaluating embedding + reranking flow for product search across web + docs. Primary concerns: throughput at 500-2k QPS, integration with existing vector DB (Milvus currently), embedding dimensionality trade-offs (768 vs 1536), hybrid search, and data residency/SOC2. Interested in hosted to start but have enterprise requirements that may push them to Dedicated or a Private VPC deployment. Agreed to pilot and benchmark. Next step is a technical deep dive and Redwood to send pricing and benchmarks.
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-11-29 15:30 PST | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Sofia Chen, Miguel Alvarez, Ravi Patel (Redwood) -- Liam O'Connor, Priya Sharma, Daniel Wu, Aisha Khan (Nebula Labs)
[00:00] Sofia Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round of intros?
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: yeah liam here, head of search at nebula labs. we're reworking our product search and need better rerank. currently using milvus + a bm25 fallback
[00:30] Priya Sharma: priya, ml eng, i'll be doing the integration and running the benchmarks
[00:36] Daniel Wu: daniel, cto, i'm interested in cost implications and whether we'll need private infra

[00:42] Sofia Chen: great. miguel from our infra team will cover throughput and benchmarks, ravi will talk ops and security. quick thing: is the plan to do embeddings+rerank for both web results and docs?
[01:02] Liam O'Connor: yes, both. mix of short queries and long context. latency matters for web interactive, throughput during peak is a big one
[01:15] Miguel Alvarez: perfect. can you share current QPS and dataset size?

[01:21] Priya Sharma: right now avg QPS is 300 with peaks to ~1.2k. document corpus around 12M vectors, dimensionality 1536 from prior model experiments. storage is on prem, Milvus cluster managed by infra team
[01:38] Miguel Alvarez: okay 12 million is a good data point. are you using hybrid search today (bm25 + vector) or pure vector?
[01:46] Liam O'Connor: hybrid — we use bm25 for recall then vectors for rerank. sometimes we do late interaction reranking. open to changing architecture if cost/latency improves

[02:05] Sofia Chen: makes sense. couple of high-level options: 1) Redwood Hosted to get started fast — we host embeddings and rerank endpoints; 2) Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity if you need predictable throughput and isolation; 3) Redwood Private VPC/on-prem if you need full control and KMS/HSM integration. any early preference?
[02:28] Daniel Wu: we'd like to start hosted to iterate quickly, but we have SOC2 reqs and the idea of private later. is there an easy migration path?

[02:36] Ravi Patel: yes — same API surface across modes. we support pinning model versions and routing policies so migrating from hosted to dedicated/private is mostly config + data plane provisioning. some network setup for VPC though
[02:54] Priya Sharma: curious about embedding models and costs. we're currently using a 1536-dim model. would lower-dim (e.g., 768) be acceptable?

[03:05] Miguel Alvarez: depends on quality tradeoff. we usually recommend running a small eval set comparing 768 vs 1536 — embedding dimensionality often trades latency/cost vs recall. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and model/precision combos based on your evals
[03:22] Liam O'Connor: on the vector DB side, we use Milvus. we'd like to know how Redwood integrates — do you manage the vectors for us or do we keep them in our DB?

[03:33] Sofia Chen: we support both patterns. hosted mode can store embeddings in our managed vector storage or we can call out to your existing DB via connector. Dedicated and Private give you options: keep vectors in your VPC Milvus and run rerank in Redwood via secure egress, or push precomputed scores back into your system. there are tradeoffs for network round trips vs throughput
[03:56] Priya Sharma: nngh, network latency is a thing. if we keep vectors in Milvus on-prem, will rerank calls from Redwood add significant latency?

[04:07] Miguel Alvarez: typically we co-locate rerank compute near the vector DB or run a dedicated path. for high QPS (1k+), we recommend dedicated capacity in the same cloud region or a private deployment with VPC peering to minimize RTT. we can also batch requests and use async scoring in some flows
[04:28] Daniel Wu: how about throughput per GPU? ballpark numbers?

[04:33] Miguel Alvarez: depends on model size and sequence length. for a transformer-based reranker with 1536-dim embeddings feeding a cross-encoder, you might see a few hundred sync queries per second per GPU; but if you use a light-weight bi-encoder + dot-product rerank it's much higher. Redwood has benchmarked combos; i'll share the spreadsheet
[04:56] Liam O'Connor: can we do approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) in Milvus and then send top-K to Redwood for a cross-encoder rerank?

[05:04] Sofia Chen: absolutely — that hybrid flow (ANN -> cross-encoder) is common. you tune K depending on recall/latency. we also support rerank-only endpoints where you POST pairs and get scores back
[05:16] Priya Sharma: any guidance on K and cost? if top-100 into a cross encoder that's heavy
[05:23] Miguel Alvarez: yes typical K is 20-50 for good balance. cross-encoder over top-20 is common. you can also cascade: cheap scorer first, then cross-encoder for final top-10
[05:36] Aisha Khan: from product perspective we want sub-200ms p95 interactive for web search — is that realistic?
[05:44] Miguel Alvarez: with dedicated capacity co-located with your DB and a good cascade, sub-200ms p95 is achievable. hosted can get close but depends on network RTT and multi-tenant variability
[05:58] Daniel Wu: security: we need SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS for keys, and audit logs. do you support those?

[06:06] Ravi Patel: yes. Redwood has SOC2, supports SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integrations for Private. Hosted offers encryption at rest and in transit and audit logs; for HSM/KMS you’d typically look at Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS
[06:22] Priya Sharma: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? can we get something running in 2-3 weeks?
[06:28] Sofia Chen: yes for a hosted pilot we can spin up API keys and a sandbox in a few days. Dedicated or Private needs infra lead time — usually 2-6 weeks depending on approvals and network setup
[06:41] Liam O'Connor: pricing — how do you price embeddings vs rerank?

[06:46] Sofia Chen: hosted pricing is per-embedding call + per-rerank token/time or per-request SKU depending on model. Dedicated is committed capacity (monthly) with predictable unit costs. we'll send you the deck with line items and a sizing worksheet
[06:58] Priya Sharma: what about quantization? for 1536-dim vectors we can quantize to lower precision to save memory, do you recommend that?

[07:06] Miguel Alvarez: yes we recommend experimenting with 8-bit or product quantization for vector storage; tradeoffs in recall. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles. if you need exact scores for compliance, some quant profiles are not acceptable
[07:21] Liam O'Connor: on the connectors: do you have an out-of-the-box connector for Milvus?
[07:26] Sofia Chen: we have connectors / examples for Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate, and S3-based pipelines. typically we provide a sample ingestion script and a connector pattern
[07:34] Priya Sharma: ok can you send that?
[07:36] Sofia Chen: yes miguel will share the sample ingestion and benchmark scripts
[07:41] Miguel Alvarez: i'll drop a link to the benchmark spreadsheet after the call. note: the sheet includes different model profiles (512, 768, 1536 dims) and cost/latency tradeoffs we measured
[07:52] Daniel Wu: curious about model choices for embeddings — do you recommend open models or your curated ones?

[07:58] Sofia Chen: we curate open models and also host vetted ones. for embeddings, many customers use 1536-dim models for semantic recall, but smaller dims can work if you retrain or use fine-tuned models. Redwood's model catalog shows vetted quality metrics
[08:14] Liam O'Connor: regulatory: we need data residency in EU for EU traffic. can hosted guarantee that?
[08:21] Ravi Patel: hosted has regional endpoints and we can route EU traffic to EU region. for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private where vectors/data stay in your VPC or on-prem
[08:33] Priya Sharma: can you run a small eval for us — we'll provide a gold set of queries and relevance labels?
[08:38] Miguel Alvarez: yes we can run evals. Redwood Optimize can run quality comparisons across model dims and quantization. we'll need your test set and desired metrics (MRR, recall@k)
[08:49] Aisha Khan: what are the typical failure modes during migration from our current Milvus to Redwood-hosted?

[08:57] Sofia Chen: common issues are embedding model mismatch, vector normalization mismatches, and differences in ANN indexing hyperparams. we provide checklists and scripts to validate embeddings and scoring
[09:10] Liam O'Connor: let's talk SLA. for Dedicated we need uptime guarantees and incident response SLAs
[09:16] Ravi Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and response times; we can include escalation paths and runbooks in the contract
[09:25] Priya Sharma: any limits on sequence length or max tokens for rerankers? some of our docs are long

[09:31] Miguel Alvarez: cross-encoders care about token length; we recommend truncation/striding or a chunking approach. we also do KV cache management for longer contexts in generation models; for rerank, chunking is typical
[09:45] Daniel Wu: cost example: for 1k QPS with a top-20 rerank cascade, can you give a rough monthly cost?

[09:53] Sofia Chen: rough back-of-envelope depends on model choices. we'll run a sizing worksheet for you but to ballpark — depending on dedicated reservation you'd be in the low tens of thousands per month for predictable capacity; hosted could be higher variable cost during peaks
[10:10] Priya Sharma: latency with external Milvus is still a worry. could we push precomputed scores from Redwood back into Milvus to avoid cross calls?
[10:18] Miguel Alvarez: yes pushing precomputed dense features or cached rerank scores for popular items is a supported optimization. Redwood supports prefix/KV caching to reduce recompute
[10:30] Aisha Khan: for the pilot what success criteria should we agree on?

[10:35] Sofia Chen: suggested success criteria: 1) meet baseline recall improvement (X% lift on MRR), 2) p95 latency under target (200ms for interactive), 3) predictable cost under N dollars per month, 4) integration feasibility with Milvus. we'll formalize after you send the eval set
[10:52] Liam O'Connor: ok sounds good. timeline — post-call we'll share an initial pilot plan
[11:00] Sofia Chen: recap: we will send pricing deck, benchmark sheet, ingestion connector, and proposed pilot plan. miguel to run an initial evaluation once priya sends sample data
[11:12] Priya Sharma: i'll send a 10k sample of vectors and the relevance labels + target QPS by friday
[11:20] Miguel Alvarez: noted. i'll run the benchmark and share results and recommendations for dim/quant and K tuning
[11:28] Daniel Wu: any compliance docs? we'll need SOC2 and encryption detail
[11:33] Ravi Patel: i'll attach SOC2 attestation and a security checklist. if you want a security deep-dive we can schedule that
[11:40] Sofia Chen: perfect. are there any other blockers?
[11:43] Liam O'Connor: none from me, just want to see the numbers
[11:46] Aisha Khan: product team is happy with pilot plan
[11:48] Sofia Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and links. expect the deck + spreadsheet within 48 hours
[11:55] End of meeting
